title: Absence of barren plateaus and scaling of gradients in the energy optimization of isometric tensor network states
abstract: Proves that variational optimization of matrix product states (MPS), tree tensor networks (TTN), and the multiscale entanglement renormalization ansatz (MERA) are free of barren plateaus for extensive Hamiltonians with finite-range interactions. Establishes analytical gradient variance scaling guarantees using Riemannian optimization framework with Haar-random initialization. Key result: MERA gradient variance scales polynomially (not exponentially) with system size, providing mathematical trainability guarantee for tensor-network-based VQE.
key_claims: MERA optimization is provably free of barren plateaus
Gradient variance scales polynomially with system size for MERA
Same guarantee holds for MPS and tree tensor networks
Provides analytical motivation for specific initialization schemes
Published in Communications in Mathematical Physics (2025)
